name: textset
algorithm: Overwrite of a reusable heap string: per round a fresh string, then n times the next splitmix64 value v picks k = v % 300 bytes at offset (v >> 16) % 3796 of a 4,096-byte lowercase source, the string is set to them (capacity kept), and the checksum adds its length, 7 times its first byte and its last byte (README.md).

skip.c: no growable string in C's standard library
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum folds every set string's length and two of its bytes
notes: The overwrite: Mk HeapText.Set over the process heap; Rust String::clear then push_str; Zig std.ArrayList(u8) clearRetainingCapacity then appendSlice over std.heap.smp_allocator; Go append(b[:0], s...) on a []byte (strings.Builder.Reset drops its buffer). Each keeps its capacity, so after the first few sets no column allocates.
Mk and Rust check that both ends of src[off..off + k] are character boundaries; Go and Zig slice bytes.
